about: The Church remembers Christ's blessed Passion, Resurrection, and glorious Ascension. From the gifts received from God, it offers to His majesty a pure Victim, a holy Victim, a spotless Victim, the holy Bread of eternal life and the Chalice of everlasting salvation.

seg.tr: Therefore, O Lord, we, Your servants, and likewise Your holy people, mindful of the blessed Passion of the same Christ, Your Son, our Lord, of His Resurrection from the dead, and of His glorious Ascension into heaven:

fn.w001: A connective joining this prayer to the preceding text: wherefore.
fn.w006: In apposition to “nos” (w005): we, thy servants.
fn.w009: “Sed et” extends the subject from “nos servi tui” to “plebs tua sancta”.
fn.w021: The first of the three genitives depending on “mémores” (w003).
fn.w023: The phrase “nec non” forms a unit meaning and also.
fn.w026: An ablative plural after “ab” (w025). The phrase “ab ínferis” depends on “resurrectiónis” (w027).
fn.w031: The accusative plural of “cælum”. The noun is masculine in the plural.

seg.tr: offer to Your excellent majesty, from Your own gifts and all that You have bestowed upon us,

fn.w034: The finite verb whose subject is the earlier “nos servi tui, sed et plebs tua sancta”.
fn.w042: The participle of “do” used as a noun: things given. It is joined to “donis” (w040).

seg.nr: The priest joins his hands and makes three signs of the cross over the Host and chalice together.

seg.tr: a pure Victim, a holy Victim, a spotless Victim,

fn.w043: “Hóstia” means a sacrifice or sacrificial victim.

seg.nr: The priest makes one sign of the cross over the Host.

seg.tr: the holy Bread of eternal life

seg.nr: The priest makes one sign of the cross over the chalice.

seg.tr: and the Chalice of everlasting salvation.
